description_full: Eaton Corporation plc operates as a power management company in the United States, Canada, Latin America, Europe, and the Asia Pacific. It operates through Electrical Americas, Electrical Global, Aerospace, Vehicle, and eMobility segments. The company offers electrical and industrial components, power distribution and assemblies, residential products, single- and three-phase power quality and connectivity products, wiring devices, circuit protection products, utility power distribution products, and power reliability equipment; and hazardous duty electrical equipment, emergency lighting, fire detection, intrinsically safe explosion-proof instrumentation, and structural support systems. It also provides pumps, motors, hydraulic power units, hoses and fittings, and electro-hydraulic pumps; valves, cylinders, electronic controls, electromechanical actuators, sensors, aircraft flap and slat systems, and nose wheel steering systems; hose and thermoplastic tubing products, fittings, adapters, couplings, and sealing and ducting products; air-to-air refueling systems, fuel pumps, fuel inerting products, sensors, and adapters and regulators; oxygen generation systems, payload carriages, and thermal management products; wiring connectors and cables; and hydraulic and bag filters, strainers and cartridges, and golf grips for manufacturers of commercial and military aircraft, related aftermarket customers, and industrial applications. In addition, the company offers transmissions, clutches, hybrid power systems, superchargers, engine valves and valve actuation systems, locking and limited slip differentials, transmission controls, and fuel vapor components for the vehicle industry; and voltage inverters, converters, fuses, circuit protection units, vehicle controls, power distribution systems, fuel tank isolation valves, and commercial vehicle hybrid systems. The company was formerly known as Abeiron Limited. The company was founded in 1911 and is based in Dublin, Ireland.

financial_summary: Eaton Corporation, PLC is a large-cap industrials business with a $137.1B market cap on $27.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 13% against a 10% cost of capital, a 3-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $3.6B in free cash flow — roughly 13 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.09× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.3× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 20× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.5% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

prof: ROIC of 13% earns above the cost of capital of 9.6%, but the 3pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have been steady (CV 0.21).

hlth: Leverage is conservative at 1.3x net debt to EBITDA ($803.0M of cash against $8.8B of debt), with interest covered 20.5x.

growth: Revenue has compounded at 9.8% over 3 years and 9.0% over 5 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 6.8% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.07 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 56% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 49%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (0.9x, 3.3% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 22, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.1%), and institutions hold 87%.
Insider trading is two-way: 4 purchases and 5 sales over the past year, net $15.8M sold.
It returns 2.5% a year to shareholders (1.4% in buybacks and 1.2% in dividends).

It has paid a dividend for 53 consecutive years, raising it 6.7% a year over the last five.
